text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: SLO breach detected for dedicated pool 'eu-west-1-gpu-4' - p99 latency 3.8s over 5m window, streaming stalls up to 15%. Root cause suspected: autoscaler delay / pool saturation. See metrics: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/1778912345
aj: on it. Acknowledging. Which customers impacted?
maria: seeing queue depth spike to 240 requests (limit 200) around 09:12 UTC, CPU/GPU util at 98% on pool nodes. Autoscaler logs show backoff & failed scale attempts: `scale_attempts=3, last_error=timeout_attach`
ryan: p95 ~ 0.9s but p99 ~ 3.8s, tails show streaming stalls (stall length ~ 4-12s). Some requests show repeated resend/stream chunks.
aj: initial mitigations I can do: 1) increase pool by 4 GPUs manually, 2) enable temporary routing to hosted fallback for non-SLA tenants, 3) throttle burst for new sessions. Which first?
maria: increase pool ASAP. Autoscaler seems stuck because of AZ-level capacity in eu-west-1. Manual resize might also hit same limit but worth trying to request capacity from infra. Also warmup is an issue — cold hosts show KV cache misses causing initial token generation latency.
aj: running manual scale now:```bash
rictl pool resize --pool eu-west-1-gpu-4 --add 4 --reason "incident manual scaling"
```
devops-bot: Action queued: request sent to cloud provider, request id cp-6f8a2. Estimated time 6-9 minutes for attachments.
ryan: while we wait, recommend enabling fallback routing for burst traffic and reducing concurrency per-worker to reduce queuing.
aj: toggling routing policy to route non-enterprise orgs to hosted model and limiting per-tenant qps to 15 for 10m.```yaml
route_policy:
  name: emergency-burst-shed
  match: non_enterprise
  action: route_to: hosted/redwood-small-v2
  rate_limit: 15/s
```
els: (system) Policy applied: emergency-burst-shed now active for non_enterprise.
maria: started issuing warmup calls to new hosts to populate KV cache:```python
for i in range(50):
  client.generate(model='redwood/med-v1', prompt='warmup', max_tokens=1)
```
aj: good. also enabling short TTL prefix cache for 1h to help reuse common completions.
sam_cs: flagged top 3 impacted customers: org-334 (chat product), org-129 (search embeddings), org-501 (support bot). Opening CS tickets and sending proactive notices.
sam_cs: note: org-334 reported user facing stalls from 09:10 UTC. They are on Dedicated plan — prioritize their SLA.
aj: for SLA customers, enabling bypass to fallback within same region if capacity constrained. Also increasing therapeutic retry window for streaming clients from 500ms to 800ms to reduce duplicate traffic.
ryan: logs show many `kv.miss` on first 2 tokens causing 120-300ms extra per token on cold hosts. But tail stalls are coming from blocked inference threads waiting on queue slots -> stack traces show `request_wait` durations >5s.
maria: autoscaler logs: `scale_cooldown: 60s`, `max_add: 2` - so autoscaler limited to small increments and cool-down; with sudden burst we hit limit then queue grows. We should tune emergency path to allow larger immediate adds.
aj: agreed — for incidents we should have emergency override. Filing infra task after incident to add an emergency flag. For now manual scaling + routing should mitigate.
devops-bot: Cloud provider attachments succeeded. 4 new nodes started attaching (node-664, node-665, node-666, node-667). Warmup in progress.
aj: seeing drop in queue depth now to ~80. p99 trending down to 1.2s. Streaming stalls still at ~6% but improving.
ryan: confirming: p95=0.85s p99=1.2s stream_stalls=6% over last 2m. Good trend.
els: (system) Scheduled oncall handoff: aj -> elaine at 09:30 UTC.
aj: logging actions taken: manual pool resize + warmup calls + route policy emergency-burst-shed + per-tenant throttle. Creating incident ticket: INC-2026-1778912345. Assigning postmortem to infra/serving -> maria + ryan.
maria: collecting traces/evicted requests, saving KV cache warmup script to incident artifacts.
elaine: I'll take over at handoff; any outstanding items?
aj: monitor p99 for 15m, verify fallback routing did not break enterprise tenants, ensure no regression in token generation correctness. Sam_cs to follow up with customers.
sam_cs: initial customer notices sent to org-334 and org-129; CS will await root cause before broader communication.
ryan: recommend action items post-incident: 1) add emergency autoscale override (allow +8 nodes immediate), 2) reduce autoscaler cooldown & increase max_add for dedicated pools, 3) add pre-warm flow for newly attached nodes (nop requests), 4) add better queue depth alerting (p99 queue_wait > 2s).
maria: will draft postmortem and include graphs: queue depth, attach times, p95/p99, stream stall rate, hot vs cold host breakdown.
devops-bot: Incident INC-2026-1778912345 created and linked to ticket tracker.
elaine: taking oncall. Thanks team — keep me posted if p99 rises again.
aj: closing thread for now, will reopen if regressions. :white_check_mark:
